subject.title: fix(compaction): prevent repeated restarts after safety timeouts

question: Should a wrapper-owned compaction safety timeout permit exactly one explicitly marked partial compaction result to commit during the bounded settlement window after timeout cancellation?
rationale: The patch changes when timed-out work may become authoritative persisted session state; tests can prove the bounds, but only maintainers can choose whether that post-timeout state policy is acceptable.

options.title: Accept bounded partial commit
options.body: Approve the marked-result and reason-owned settlement-token policy after restoring the shared timeout dependency and validating late, unmarked, external-abort, and sibling-runtime cases.

options.title: Require pre-timeout checkpointing
options.body: Reject post-timeout commits and redesign compaction so completed progress becomes authoritative before the wrapper timeout, likely through stage checkpoints or another canonical persistence boundary.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Retain current timeout semantics and close or substantially narrow this PR, leaving users to increase the existing timeout or start a new session.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded partial commit
recommendation.body: Approve the marked-result and reason-owned settlement-token policy after restoring the shared timeout dependency and validating late, unmarked, external-abort, and sibling-runtime cases.
